notes: Route: Yoast sitemap index. robots.txt (HTTP 200, permissive: 'User-Agent: * / Disallow:') advertises https://www.theclinic.cl/sitemap_index.xml, which lists 307 sub-sitemaps including 195 numbered post sitemaps (post-sitemap.xml = oldest/2010, post-sitemap195.xml = newest), ~1000 <url> entries each with <loc> + <lastmod>. Walked from the highest number downwards, stopping when a file's NEWEST date is already before the window. That needed only 3 requests: 195 (323 urls, 2026-08-28..2026-10-25 -> 322 in window), 194 (1000 urls, 2009..2026-10-18 -> rest of window), 193 (newest 2026-09-15, all older -> stop). Total run 2s, 4 requests. IMPORTANT pitfall: the first version stopped on a file's MINIMUM date and quit after 195 alone, because sitemap195 contains one recently-updated 2026-08-28 post; break on the max date, not the min. Date = the day permalink /YYYY/MM/DD/ in every article URL (site's own Chile-local publication date), <lastmod> only as fallback (not needed here: 0 urls lacked a day permalink). Verified on 12 articles across 6 days: HTTP 200, article:published_time == JSON-LD datePublished, and local date equal to the listed date (a 2026-09-30 21:04 local story carries 2026-10-01T00:04:10+00:00 in the UTC meta, i.e. exactly the 1-day tolerance). Body text after tag-stripping was 4553-13694 chars per article, so the 1500-char gate passes with room. Result: 1014 unique URLs, all 31 days covered, min 12/day, 2026-09-30 = 49, 2026-10-10 = 18, 2026-10-20 = 41. Skipped: news-sitemap.xml (only last ~2 days), archive pages and Wayback (unnecessary here).
